page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is an x86_64 cloud server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 8 threads. Driven by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the instance includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside comprehensive instruction support such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a memory-dense ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally bundled with a 480 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without integrated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark measurements show distinct performance characteristics across varied workloads. The AMD EPYC cores deliver top-tier single-threaded compression and decompression throughput, recording 39.69 GB/sec in gzip compression, 17.7 GB/sec in bzip3 single-threaded decompression, and an upper-bracket stress-ng single-core score of 3621.28. In broader compute assessments, Geekbench scores reach 1940.0 for single-core and 7489.0 for multi-core, while PassMark reports a total CPU score of 18514.04 and an encryption score of 10313.5. System memory throughput measures 71.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 41.17 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a Redis SET throughput of 15.3 million operations per second and static web throughput of 26.44 GB/sec. Small-scale model inference achieves top-tier generation speeds of 372.5 tokens per second on 135M parameters, though prompt processing on larger 7B models falls into the lower tier at 31.93 tokens per second.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation ensures consistent execution without CPU throttling or noisy-neighbor interference common to shared compute. The generous 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation and integrated NVMe solid-state storage deliver high operational density for stateful applications, eliminating the need for separate external volume configurations. The primary tradeoff lies in raw multi-core scaling, where four physical cores provide mid-range aggregate throughput compared to high-core compute-focused nodes. This hardware configuration is most effectively deployed for in-memory databases, caching layers, Redis instances, indexing pipelines, medium-scale transactional relational databases, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
description: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs over 4 physical AMD EPYC cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 480 GB local NVMe SSD. Utilizing an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, it exhibits top-tier single-core efficiency and compression throughput alongside steady mid-tier multi-core execution. The high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per core supports memory-resident operations, reflected by Redis throughput exceeding 15.3 million operations per second and uncached memory read bandwidth of 71.86 GB/sec. While larger machine learning prompt processing is constrained by core counts, the dedicated CPU allocation and local high-speed storage provide steady performance for stateful applications. The configuration is primarily tailored for in-memory data caching, transactional database engines, search indexing, and data processing pipelines that require predictable memory density and low-latency disk storage without dedicated GPU hardware.
